b: Geography: North America (Mississippi/Ohio valleys + Great Lakes region)
Primary pulmonary infection → can disseminate to skin (most common extrapulmonary site), bone, genitourinary tract, CNS
Pathology: mixed suppurative and granulomatous inflammation; thick-walled, broad-based budding yeast — pathognomonic
More likely to cause symptomatic/progressive disease than Histoplasma
In tissue: large thick-walled single budding yeast cells with broad connections between parent and bud
Infection starts in lungs, disseminates to skin, bone, genitourinary tract
NOT endemic to South America — that is Paracoccidioides
NOT equally in men and women — males more affected

qs.q: The most common extrapulmonary site of dissemination in blastomycosis is
qs.e: Skin is the most common extrapulmonary site of blastomycosis dissemination. Contrast with coccidioidomycosis where meningeal involvement is the most serious complication, and histoplasmosis where liver, spleen, and adrenals are affected.

qs.q: Which statement about blastomycosis is correct?
o: One finds large thick-walled single budding yeast cells with broad connections
This systemic infection occurs with equal frequency in both men and women
The infection starts in the skin and organisms disseminate to the lungs
The infectious disease is endemic to certain rural areas of South America
qs.e: The pathognomonic tissue finding of blastomycosis is large, thick-walled yeast cells with a single broad-based bud. Blastomycosis primarily affects males, starts in the lungs, and is endemic to North America.

qs.q: Which statement about blastomycosis is correct? Broad-based budding is the hallmark microscopic feature of Blastomyces dermatitidis in tissue. ---
o: In tissue one finds large thick-walled single budding yeast cells
Occurs equally in men and women like other endemic mycoses
All reported clinical cases require treatment with amphotericin B
Disease is endemic to certain geographical areas of South America
Infection starts in the skin and disseminates to visceral organs
qs.e: Blastomyces dermatitidis is classically identified in tissue by large, thick-walled yeast cells with broad-based budding.
